outcomes.original: Filing step: Engage a liquor license broker to identify and secure a Type 48 license from another bar located within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District that is willing to transfer. What to say: Tell the broker the license must come from a bar (Type 48 holder) currently located within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District boundaries, as required by Planning Code Section 249.60(b)(2)(C). Confirm the source location and that the seller has no outstanding ABC violations. Do not close on the license purchase until Planning has issued the Conditional Use Authorization, because the CUA is required before ABC will approve the transfer. Make the lease contingent on obtaining both the CUA and the license transfer approval.
outcomes.note: The record confirms the district and code section but does not contain the rule text or the specific transfer and CUA requirements cited.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File a Conditional Use Authorization application with San Francisco Planning for a bar use at 200 Capp St, referencing the Type 48 license transfer from within the Mission SUD. What to say: State that the bar will use a Type 48 license transferred from [source address within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD]. Commit to all Planning Code Section 202.2 operating conditions: appoint a community liaison, post a contact telephone number, implement a good-neighbor policy including soundproofing and litter control within a one-block radius. Commit to the Section 249.60(d) facade and lighting requirements: provide outside lighting, limit window signage to 33% of window area, and maintain 50% clear glazing on street-facing facades. Propose operating hours (state the proposed closing time; expect the Commission may condition it). Describe the concept as a neighborhood bar with recorded music, no food service, and no live entertainment or dancing. Include a sound study if the space shares walls or floors with residential units.
outcomes.note: The records confirm CUA requirement and license transfer within Mission SUD but do not state the specific Section 202.2 or 249.60(d) requirements, Commission conditioning of hours, or sound study requirement.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File a building permit application with DBI for tenant improvements and exterior signage, routing it to Planning for zoning review under Planning Code Section 175. What to say: Submit plans showing the bar layout, finishes, any structural or mechanical work, and the occupant load calculation. Attach the approved CUA. If the occupant load is 50 or more, the space is Assembly Group A-2 and the permit must address accessibility, exits, and fire-safety systems for that group. If fewer than 50, it is Group B. Identify the existing occupancy group and whether a change of occupancy is triggered; if so, the permit must bring the space into full code compliance for the new group. Route the sign permit through Planning for compliance with Article 6 sign controls.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $3,100 to $15,000. Notes: The day and cost ranges cover the Conditional Use Authorization (120 to 300 days, $3,100 to $15,000 per the catalog) from filing to Commission approval, which is the critical path. These are times and costs to approval for the CUA. ABC license transfer (90 to 180 days, cost depends on the purchase price of the license from the seller, typically $100,000 to $450,000 in San Francisco) and the building permit (14 to 120 days, $800 to $15,000) run in parallel or follow the CUA. The CUA timeline depends on pre-application meetings, environmental review, hearing scheduling, and any appeals; the catalog estimates 120 to 300 days. The building permit depends on the scope of tenant improvements and plan completeness. Government fees for the CUA, building permit, business registration, sign permit, and health permit total roughly $4,000 to $17,000; the Type 48 license purchase from another bar is the largest cost but is paid to a private seller, not a government agency, so it is not included in the cost range shown here. If the count of eating and drinking uses in NCT-MISSION is already at or above the 179-unit cap, the CUA may not be grantable, in which case no time or cost to approval can be given until Planning confirms the count.
